anf_compare.notes: No ANF or other public-domain English of this homily; translated from the Greek.

bible_refs.note: οἱ πυλωροὶ τοῦ ᾅδου θεωρήσαντες ἔπτηξαν echoes Job 38:17 LXX (πυλωροὶ δὲ ᾅδου ἰδόντες σε ἔπτηξαν); cited inline.
»Ἰησοῦν ζητεῖτε opens the angels' words of Mark 16:6; the quotation runs on into u01-rem-mid, where the citation stands.

choices.term: οὗτος ὡς θεὸς τὸν θάνατον ἐσκύλευσεν
choices.english: this same one, as God, stripped death of its spoils
choices.why: ὡς marks what he is, not a likeness: he is God, not like God. σκυλεύω is to strip a fallen enemy of his spoils.
rejected: This man, like God, has overcome death

choices.term: εἷς γὰρ ὢν ὁ σαρκωθεὶς Λόγος εἰς ἓν ταῦτα κἀκεῖνα ὡς ἠβουλήθη ἀρρήτῳ λόγῳ συνήγαγεν
choices.english: For the Word made flesh, being one, brought these things and those together into one, as he willed, in a manner beyond telling
choices.why: Keeps every element of the clause: 'being one', 'into one', 'as he willed' and the play on Λόγος / λόγῳ.
rejected: the Logos, who became flesh, has united these things in an ineffable way

choices.term: τὴν μὲν σάρκα διακονῆσαι τοῖς πάθεσι δέδωκεν
choices.english: He gave his flesh to serve the sufferings
choices.why: διακονῆσαι is an infinitive of purpose with the dative τοῖς πάθεσι: the flesh is given over to bear the sufferings.

choices.english: Otherwise, how do angels minister at a tomb
choices.why: Read as ἐπεὶ πῶς, a question in the series πὼς δὲ ... πὼς δὲ: only God's presence explains the angels.
rejected: since angels somehow serve as attendants at the tomb

choices.term: πὼς δὲ λευχείμονες ὡς ἐπὶ νυμφίῳ ταῖς γυναιξὶν ἐμφανίζονται
choices.english: how do they appear in white to the women, as for a bridegroom
choices.why: λευχείμονες describes the angels, the subject; ταῖς γυναιξὶν is the dative of those to whom they appear.
rejected: the women, like brides, appear to them

pass_a_gloss: [continuing from the previous section: but the one buried as] a man, this one as God despoiled (σκυλεύω) death. Again, as dead the soldiers (στρατιῶται) guarded (φρουρέω) [him], and as God the gatekeepers (πυλωροί) of Hades, having beheld, cowered (πτήσσω). The same, this one and that one, you will call [him], not other and other, nor other in other, nor other through other; for being one, the enfleshed (σαρκόω) Word (λόγος) into one these things and those, as he willed, by an unspeakable (ἄρρητος) word brought together (συνάγω); and the flesh on the one hand he has given to serve (διακονέω) the sufferings, the Godhead (θεότης) on the other he has used toward the signs and the wonders; but just as [it is] not lawful (θεμιτός) for the Word to be parted from the flesh, so [it is] necessary for the sufferings (πάθημα) to have been woven together (συμπλέκω) with the wonders (θαῦμα). For the one who as dead went down to Hades, this one as God freed (ἐλευθερόω) the dead; since how do angels serve a tomb, and how do white-robed ones (λευχείμων), as at a bridegroom, show themselves (ἐμφανίζω) to the women, and how did they say to them: 'Jesus you seek' [continues in the next section]
pass_b_english: …this same one, as God, stripped death of its spoils. Again, the soldiers kept guard over him as one dead, and the gatekeepers of Hades, beholding him as God, cowered (Job 38:17).

You will say that this one and that one are the same, not one and another, nor one in another, nor one through another. For the Word made flesh, being one, brought these things and those together into one, as he willed, in a manner beyond telling. He gave his flesh to serve the sufferings, and he made use of his Godhead for the signs and wonders; but as it is not right for the Word to be separated from the flesh, so the sufferings must be interwoven with the wonders. For he who went down into Hades as one dead, this same one as God set the dead free. Otherwise, how do angels minister at a tomb, how do they appear in white to the women, as for a bridegroom, and how did they say to them, 'You are looking for Jesus…'
source_text:
ἄνθρωπος οὗτος ὡς θεὸς τὸν θάνατον ἐσκύ λευσεν. Πάλιν ὡς νεκρὸν οἱ στρατιῶται
ἐφρούρησαν καὶ ὡς θεὸν οἱ πυλωροὶ τοῦ ᾅδου θεωρήσαντες ἔπτηξαν.
3 Τὸν αὐτὸν δὲ τοῦτον κἀκεῖνον ἐρεῖς, οὐκ ἄλλον καὶ ἄλλον, οὐδὲ ἄλλον ἐν
ἄλλῳ, οὐδὲ ἄλλον δι' ἄλλου· εἷς γὰρ ὢν ὁ σαρκω θεὶς Λόγος εἰς ἓν ταῦτα κἀκεῖνα ὡς
ἠβουλήθη ἀρρήτῳ λόγῳ συνήγαγεν· καὶ τὴν μὲν σάρκα διακονῆσαι τοῖς πάθεσι
δέδωκεν, τῇ θεότητι δὲ πρὸς τὰ σημεῖα καὶ τὰ θαύματα κέχρηται, ἀλλ' ὥσπερ οὐ
θεμιτὸν τὸν Λόγον ἐκ τῆς σαρκὸς χωρίζεσθαι, οὕτως ἀνάγκη τὰ παθήματα
συμπεπλέχθαι τοῖς θαύμασιν. Ὁ γὰρ ὡς νεκρὸς εἰς ᾅδου καταβάς, οὗτος ὡς θεὸς τοὺς
νεκροὺς ἠλευθέρωσεν, ἐπεί πως τάφῳ διακονοῦσιν ἄγγελοι, πὼς δὲ λευχείμονες ὡς
ἐπὶ νυμφίῳ ταῖς γυναιξὶν ἐμφανίζονται, πὼς δὲ πρὸς αὐτὰς ἔλεγον· »Ἰησοῦν ζητεῖτε
